description: We are a team of enthusiastic students passionate about technology, space exploration, and innovation. Our goal is to gain hands-on experience in hackathons, understand the regional and international competition environment, and strengthen our skills through practical project development. We aim to explore coding, game development, research, and problem-solving. We welcome motivated teammates with interests in programming, UI/UX design, space science, and creative thinking.
summary:
CYGNOVA Mission Forge

CYGNOVA — Mission Forge is an interactive browser-based space mission design game created for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. It gives players a way to explore decisions involved in planning and operating a space mission. Players begin by choosing one of three mission scenarios: Earth Blue Watch, Moon Polar Echo, or Mars Red Horizon. They then select a rocket, choose one to three science tools, and set an orbit.

After launch, the game takes players through a countdown, ascent, transit, and orbital operations. During the mission, players encounter two decision alerts and choose a SAFE or BOLD response. These choices affect the mission outcome and encourage players to consider risk, scientific value, spacecraft condition, and limited resources. At the end, the game evaluates performance using science results, spacecraft health, and cost efficiency, with a score of up to three stars.

Mission references include NASA missions and orbital information associated with Landsat 9, the Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter, and the Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter. Fictional values are identified as such. Built with HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, and Canvas 2D, CYGNOVA combines interactive gameplay, launch animations, procedural planet generation, sound, scoring, and mission reports to make space mission planning engaging and accessible for learners.
details:
CYGNOVA — Mission Forge

CYGNOVA — Mission Forge is an interactive educational space mission design game developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 under the Space Mission Design Game challenge. Its main purpose is to help users understand how real-world space missions are planned by allowing them to make mission-related decisions through an engaging simulation.

The game offers three mission scenarios:

  • Earth — Blue Watch: Monitor Earth's climate, oceans, and land.
  • Moon — Polar Echo: Search for hidden water ice in dark lunar polar craters.
  • Mars — Red Horizon: Study minerals and atmospheric conditions on Mars.

Players begin by selecting a destination and then choosing a rocket, scientific instruments, and an appropriate orbit. They must carefully manage important mission resources, including budget, rocket capacity, power consumption, and daily data requirements. Different rockets, instruments, and orbital choices have different costs and capabilities, requiring players to balance performance with available resources.

After completing the mission configuration, players launch their spacecraft and experience different mission stages, including countdown, ascent, transit, and orbital operations. During the mission, two unexpected decision events challenge players to choose between SAFE and BOLD actions. These decisions influence the mission outcome. At the end, the game evaluates performance through a scoring system based on scientific results, spacecraft health, and cost efficiency, awarding up to three stars.

Benefits and Intended Impact:

CYGNOVA makes complex space mission planning concepts easier to understand through practical interaction rather than theory alone. It encourages critical thinking, decision-making, resource management, problem-solving, and an interest in space exploration. Students and beginners can explore the challenges of mission design in an accessible and engaging environment.

Creativity and Innovation:

The project combines space science with interactive game mechanics. Instead of simply presenting information about planets and spacecraft, it allows users to experience the consequences of their own mission-planning decisions. Its multiple destinations, rocket choices, scientific instruments, orbit configurations, mission events, visual animations, and performance reports create a replayable learning experience.

Tools and Technologies:

The project was developed using HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, and Canvas 2D. HTML provides the structure, CSS handles the interface and visual styling, JavaScript controls the game logic and interactions, and Canvas 2D supports visual scenes and animations. The game also includes sound effects and a downloadable mission report.

NASA References and Project Considerations:

The project incorporates educational reference information from NASA missions, including Landsat 9, the Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO), and the Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter (MRO). Real NASA mission orbital information is distinguished from fictional teaching values used for gameplay. The team considered mission objectives, scientific usefulness, resource limitations, spacecraft capacity, power requirements, cost, risk, accessibility, and user engagement while designing the experience.

CYGNOVA — Mission Forge is an independent educational project and is not officially endorsed by NASA.
